propositions: The check_raw_git_writes gate already correctly detects attribute-form wrapper calls (e.g., core._git(...)) via the ast.Attribute branch in _wrapper_name, but this behavior was undocumented and untested, appearing to be a blind spot.
All eight existing R2 tests in test_raw_git_write_lint.py exercise only bare-name form (ast.Name), leaving attribute-form detection unpinned and vulnerable to accidental deletion in future refactors.
The _ref_lock_push.py file contains a wrapper call (push_lease_cas) that correctly does not fire because 'push' is not in MUTATION_VERBS, not because attribute detection is absent.
Four new tests must pin attribute-form detection: literal mutation verbs, receiver-shape independence, fail-closed opaque forwarding on attributes, and marker silencing on attribute calls.
The gate's module docstring must explicitly state that the name match applies to the callable attribute regardless of receiver shape, replacing the implicit 'BY NAME' coverage.
